Subject: Redwood Dedicated demo request — Finly throughput & latency

Hi Marissa,

We signed up for a trial and are evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a production deployment. We're primarily focused on throughput and p95 latency for our realtime inference path. A few details up front:

- Expected sustained load: 150–250 QPS (spiky peaks to ~350 QPS)
- Typical request size: ~1200 tokens input, max generation ~300 tokens
- Target p95 latency: <= 200ms (preferably closer to 150ms)
- Typical concurrency: 80–120 concurrent users during peak windows

We'd like to schedule a dedicated demo that dives into capacity sizing, batching/latency tradeoffs, and autoscaling behavior. Ideally the call includes someone who can speak to the serving runtime and autoscaling (throughput/latency tradeoffs) and someone for pricing/contract questions.

Can you share availability next week? Our time zone is PT — mornings work best.

Thanks,
Priya Shah

Hi Priya — glad to meet the team. A couple of quick technical clarifications so we can make the demo actionable:

1) Are the ~1200 tokens mostly prompt/context (single-turn) or do you expect long multi-turn histories per request?
2) Do you have a test corpus or synthetic traffic profile we can run during the session? CSV works fine.
3) Any hard constraints on cold-start latency vs warmed state (e.g., do you need warm VMs all the time or can we use burst capacity)?

To set expectations: for Dedicated GPU pools with the model profiles you're exploring, we've seen customers hit ~200 QPS with p95 in the 120–180ms range when using aggressive batching + KV cache and a tuned kernel selection (depends on model and sequence length distribution). Autoscaling policies control whether additional nodes spin up for sustained load vs short bursts. We'll cover a few concrete configurations in the demo and run some back-of-envelope sizing based on your load CSV.

Proposed demo slots (PT):
- Tue Jul 21, 10:00–11:00 AM PT (preferred)
- Wed Jul 22, 2:00–3:00 PM PT

I'll prepare:
- A short capacity estimate (nodes, GPU types, expected QPS)
- A checklist for pre-demo artifacts (sample requests, max sequence length, expected concurrency)
- A runbook for the POC and suggested autoscaling policy

Marissa — I'll create the calendar invite once Priya confirms.

Thanks,
